Between August 31 and September 3, most POY grades posted a steady upward drift in domestic Chinese trading.
POY 150D/96F rose nearly 4 per cent to $1.406/kg, while POY 75D/96F climbed to $1.541/kg.

title: China's VSF surge of 1.74% puts Asia's fibre cost balance at risk
summary:
Asian VSF markets closed the week ended September 5, 2026, with regional divergence as Chinese 1.5D×38mm domestic VSF rose 1.74 per cent.
Indian 1.4D and 1.5D×38mm grades were unchanged at ₹196/kg and ₹193/kg; Pakistan’s 1.5D held at PKR 636/kg.
China’s rise narrowed intra-Asia price differentials and changed the relative attractiveness of regional sourcing routes for procurement teams.

title: Pakistan's 3.95% organic cotton jump gives India a cost edge
summary:
Pakistan’s KCA spot rate for Above-26 mm organic cotton rose 3.95 per cent on September 1 to 704.7696 PKR/kg, then held through Friday.
India’s Shankar-6 organic cotton stayed at ₹226/kg, while pre-consumer recycled cotton remained at ₹151/kg.
The move created a clear price divergence between two major Asian cotton markets despite a sharp late-week reversal in global cotton prices.

title: Is the global cotton shortage really over?
summary:
ICAC sees a thin 2026–27 cotton surplus, but USDA forecasts mill use above output and ending stocks down 7 per cent.
TexPro shows January–May raw-cotton imports across six textile markets rose 5.3 per cent, driven by China; excluding China, the other five fell 6.9 per cent.
Brazil is gaining supplier share, while firm prices keep mills cautious on availability.

title: JCRA raises India’s sovereign credit rating to A-
summary:
JCRA has raised India’s sovereign rating to A- from BBB+, putting the country back in A-grade territory after its last A-level rating in 1988.
The move follows 2025 upgrades by Morningstar DBRS, R&I and S&P, widening overseas recognition of stronger fundamentals.
For exporters, manufacturers and lenders, higher sovereign credit standing can influence borrowing costs and investor appetite.

title: Vietnam sets clearer licensing rules for foreign-invested e-commerce
summary:
Vietnam has issued Decree No. 342/2026/ND-CP, clarifying licensing and market access rules for foreign-invested trading and e-commerce businesses. 
The decree covers intermediary and integrated e-commerce platforms and social networks engaged in e-commerce. 
Provincial People’s Committees will handle licensing, while investors must meet treaty, tax, security and sector-specific requirements.

title: North India cotton yarn remains stable amid new arrival season
summary:
Cotton yarn prices stayed unchanged in Ludhiana and Delhi as north India demand cooled and buyers turned cautious before the cotton marketing season. 
Panipat recycled yarn saw average demand; cotton comber and recycled polyester fibre steadied after last week’s ₹3-5 per kg rise. 
New cotton arrivals in Haryana and Rajasthan pushed prices down by ₹50-60 per maund, with Punjab arrivals negligible.

title: Pakistan's BCI cotton jump 4.21% puts India's yarn edge in focus
summary:
Asia’s domestic cotton benchmarks moved in sharply different directions from August 31 to September 4, 2026, showing distinct price-formation mechanisms.
Pakistan’s BCI KCA Spot rose 4.21 per cent after a KCA revision, while China’s BCI 3128B fell 1.25 per cent as Xinjiang’s new crop pressured prices.
India’s BCI Shankar-6 stayed unchanged at ₹199.00/kg, reflecting MSP support.

title: EU Council approves customs reform with tougher e-commerce rules
summary:
The EU Council has approved a major customs reform introducing tougher e-commerce rules, stronger controls and a new EU customs authority. 
Non-EU platforms will become responsible for customs duties and formalities, while a handling fee on small parcels will begin in November 2026. 
The reforms will also reward highly compliant traders with simplified procedures.

title: UKFT partners with F2F to strengthen UK textile sourcing intelligence
summary:
UKFT has partnered with Fibre2Fashion to support UK’s fashion brands and textile businesses with vital sourcing insights and intelligence via the AI powered solution TexPro.
This smart intelligence system will deliver critical sourcing, trade, competitor and real-time market insights to help firms make better decisions, identify key opportunities, assess challenges and navigate global supply chains.

title: US apparel imports are weak; so why did bookings jump 79%?
summary:
US HS61–62 apparel imports fell 7.77 per cent to $36.90 billion in H1 2026, but the contraction narrowed from 11.82 per cent in Q1 to 3.28 per cent in Q2.
Clothing and accessories-store sales rose 5.9 per cent to $151.09 billion; June's inventory-to-sales ratio fell to 2.14.
US-bound HS61–62 ocean bookings reached 21,434 TEU in June, up 79 per cent, led by Vietnam and Cambodia.

title: Australia’s apparel imports dip 7.5% in July 2026
summary:
Australia’s apparel imports fell 7.57 per cent to Au$1.025 billion in July 2026; textile yarn, fabrics and made-up imports eased 2.58 per cent.
Fibre imports edged up to Au$12 million, while textile fibre exports declined 9.92 per cent to Au$629 million, Australian Bureau of Statistics data showed.
Fiscal 2025–26 saw apparel imports down 4.60 per cent and fibre exports up 7.72 per cent.

title: Bangladesh’s RMG sector bets on technology for a productivity edge
summary:
Bangladesh apparel exporters are adopting digital monitoring, data-driven production and AI tools to raise productivity, reduce downtime and improve quality.
Some factories report gains of up to 25 per cent versus manual monitoring, though results vary by technology, conditions and measurement.
The shift also raises concerns over worker pressure, privacy and fair sharing of productivity gains.

title: Jordan’s clothing exports rise 1.8% to $1.19 bn in H1 2026
summary:
Jordan’s apparel and clothing accessory exports rose 1.8 per cent year on year to JOD 846.6 million (~$1.19 billion) in H1 2026.
Knitted apparel grew 3.0 per cent to JOD 830.7 million and made up more than 98 per cent of clothing exports.
Woven apparel exports fell 36.4 per cent, while knitted and woven apparel imports rose 2.4 per cent in H1.

title: RMG exports from B’desh in green zone as shipment jumps in August 2026
summary:
Bangladesh's RMG exports rose 5.12 per cent to $7.495 billion in July-August 2026, backed by a strong August, EPB provisional data show. 
Knitwear grew 6.17 per cent to $4.193 billion, while woven apparel increased 3.81 per cent to $3.301 billion. 
Home textile exports gained 11.17 per cent to $154.55 million, but cotton and cotton products fell 13.02 per cent to $82.24 million.

title: As Sri Lanka’s exports grow, is apparel losing momentum?
summary:
Sri Lanka’s combined merchandise and services exports reached $10.49 billion in January–July 2026, up 5.48 per cent year-on-year. 
Apparel and textiles fell 6.50 per cent to $2.88 billion, diverging from broader export growth. 
July apparel and textile exports dropped 8.8 per cent to $437.59 million, with shipments declining across the United States, European Union and United Kingdom.

title: A meeting that highlights the fraying edges of Bangladesh’s RMG story
summary:
BGMEA told the President that nearly 400 garment factories have closed in Bangladesh over three years, as production costs rose almost 40 per cent. 
Inadequate gas supplies, higher energy tariffs, wages and bank interest rates are forcing many factories to operate below half capacity. 
Garment exports contracted 1.64 per cent in FY2025-26 and fell 1.92 per cent in July of FY2026-27.

title: US' PVH Corp Q2 FY26 revenue hits $2.1 bn, profit tops estimate
summary:
PVH’s Q2 FY26 revenue fell 3 per cent to $2.10 billion, but non-GAAP EPS of $3.70 beat guidance as gross margin reached 63.0 per cent.
DTC gains in the Americas and APAC, e-commerce growth and tariff refunds offset weaker wholesale, licensing declines and EMEA pressure.
The Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger owner reaffirmed FY26 guidance, with Q3 revenue seen down low single digits YoY.

title: Canadian lululemon's Q2 FY26 profit beats despite 4% revenue decline
summary:
Lululemon’s Q2 FY26 revenue fell 4 per cent YoY to $2.42 billion, but gross margin rose to 60.5 per cent as tariff refunds supported profit.
Americas softness led the decline, with revenue down 8 per cent and comparable sales down 12 per cent; international revenue grew 4 per cent.
FY26 guidance was cut to $10.35-$10.50 billion, a 5-7 per cent fall, with Q3 sales expected to drop 10-11 per cent.

title: Bangladesh vs Pakistan: What a 36% UK apparel surge really means?
summary:
UK apparel imports from Bangladesh fell 15.9 per cent to $320.6 million in June 2026; Pakistan rose 36.3 per cent and Vietnam advanced 14.7 per cent.
H1 data shows Bangladesh still up 1.5 per cent, Pakistan down 4.8 per cent and Vietnam up 10.8 per cent.
Roughly 77 per cent of Bangladesh's June decline came from HS62 woven apparel, but TexPro does not show a simple transfer to Pakistan.
